rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosures and ban on non-refundable renewal and roommate fees
rules.requirement: Before a Berkeley landlord or agent takes a screening or application fee, they must give you a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and the maximum fee allowed under Civil Code § 1950.6(b). They can put these in the application or in a separate disclosure. A landlord also can't charge a current tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees for a roommate leaving or for adding or replacing a roommate.
rules.key_value: Fee rights statement and fee cap disclosure required; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property and rental agreements in Berkeley. The disclosure rule applies whenever an owner or agent charges an applicant a fee for a credit report or to process an application. The source states no limits by building type, size or age.
rules.penalty: Lease terms that violate the chapter can't be enforced (BMC 13.78.018).
rules.reason: Both candidates are provisions of the same ordinance, Berkeley Municipal Code chapter 13.78 (§ 13.78.010 screening fee disclosures and § 13.78.016 renewal and roommate fees), so they were merged into one record.
